items.title: Henry A. "Hank" Kmen Interview, 1963-02-13
items.q: Rossini had been played before, but they did more of Rossini.

ctx.x: They, they'd fill the balconies and, uh, much to the annoyance of a lot of the, uh, study customers because they'd chop on apples and crack nuts and, uh, all sorts of things like that. You see, there were, after the St. Charles Theater opened, well, even earlier, uh, the first American theater to be built specifically for that purpose was opened in 1823 and that was a theater on Camp Street. Sometimes called the American theater, sometimes called the Camp Street Theater. And, uh, it used, uh, mounted operas. Now,…
What about the audience now? It wouldn't be all French, certainly.
